note: Every archived file lists the exact command that produced it and the scope it proves. Commands ran in D:/Craftmine World-worktrees/godot-round2-r9-20260910 on Windows. The inspected package and engine cache live outside the repository and are identified by path and hash in the records themselves. The restaged package desktop/build/r9-restaged-preview is a copy of the round-one build with corrected licences and a bundled Git tree; it is NOT a build of the integrated round-two code.

preflight-baseline.json.command: node desktop/delivery/preflight.mjs all --evidence <file>   (run at commit e4621478, before the task K repairs)
preflight-baseline.json.proves: The eight real preflight failures recorded in docs/GODOT_CYCLE_05.md reproduce exactly at e4621478: 3 bridge byte drifts, 2 undeclared runtime files, 3 missing base manifests.
preflight-baseline.json.limits: Package and engine cache inputs were not supplied in this baseline run.

preflight-final.json.proves: Notices, base assets, LGPL provenance, engine cache bytes and the restaged package pass with 0 failures; the warnings are the documented pending-licence notes.
preflight-final.json.limits: Export check skipped (no export directory). A pass means these bytes are consistent with the manifests, not that the package is a delivery build.

preflight-final.txt.limits: Text log; the JSON record is authoritative.

release-manifest.json.proves: Client, engine, export templates, broker, bases, bridge, dependencies, licences, the pinned Git bundle and the content-boundary declaration are pinned with real bytes and SHA-256; tooling:m/tooling:n record the R1/R6 branch commits without inventing a hash.
release-manifest.json.limits: A pin of this tree plus a snapshot of the restaged package; not a build attestation.

release-manifest-create.txt.proves: Component-by-component summary of what was pinned.

release-manifest-verify.txt.proves: The restaged package matches the manifest: 0 missing, 0 mismatch, 0 unpinned, 0 forbidden, 0 links, exit 0.
release-manifest-verify.txt.limits: The manifest was created with --package, so the package files are pinned from this artefact; it proves byte identity with the recorded snapshot, not reproducibility from source.

package-pin-batch07.json.proves: Read-only byte pin of the original round-one package: 828 files, 573147733 bytes, 1 installer, missing required files listed (it predates the Git requirement).
package-pin-batch07.json.limits: Pinning proves which bytes exist; it does not prove installability or licence completeness.

licensing-check-batch07.json.proves: The original round-one package fails with 67 licence failures and 19 pending entries; this is the starting point that round two had to classify.
licensing-check-batch07.json.limits: Describes that package, not the current staging pipeline.

licensing-check.txt.proves: Human-readable failure summary of the original package.

licensing-check-repaired.json.proves: After desktop/delivery/licensing/tools/apply-package-licences.mjs, the restaged package has 0 licence failures; 19 entries remain pending-rights-review / unknown-rightsholder and the exit code is 3 (PENDING, not a pass).
licensing-check-repaired.json.limits: 0 failures means the notices and texts the offline entry requires are present; it does not mean the pending rights are resolved.

licensing-check-repaired.txt.proves: Readable pending list and the final PENDING — NOT A PASS line.

licence-repair.json.command: node desktop/delivery/licensing/tools/apply-package-licences.mjs --package desktop/build/r9-restaged-preview --guide desktop/windows-USER_GUIDE.zh-CN.md   (report copied out of the package)
licence-repair.json.proves: Exactly which texts were installed, generated or kept: 45 npm packages without a bundled licence text now point at the canonical text, the GPL-3 and canonical third-party texts were installed, the Rust notice file was generated, the stale user guide was replaced, 0 unresolved, 0 failures.
licence-repair.json.limits: It repairs the licence directory and the packaged guide only; no binary changes and no licence is applied to project code.

git-bundle-verify.json.proves: The pinned MinGit archive matches the official GitHub asset digest 82b562c9…, the wrapper reports git version 2.53.0.windows.1, and LICENSE.txt (GPL-2.0) is present.
git-bundle-verify.json.limits: Verifies the archive and the version string; it does not prove the integrated client reports content.gitInfo.source=bundled.

git-bundle-stage.json.proves: The MinGit tree was laid out as resources/git/** with bin/git.exe for R1's exe-adjacent candidate: 385 files, 109064331 bytes, and a per-file hash record in resources/git/GIT-BUNDLE.json.
git-bundle-stage.json.limits: Staging proves the layout and hashes; the runtime discovery (bundled vs pathFallback) still needs an integrated client.

boundary-client.json.proves: The restaged package satisfies the client content boundary: 1233 entries, required notices present, no forbidden path (no credentials, node_modules, .git, logs, user data).
boundary-client.json.limits: The check reads names and sizes only; it does not open payload files.

size-with-git.json.proves: Real size after bundling Git: total 651.121 MB, 1233 files, resources/git 104.074 MB, all inside the frozen caps.
size-with-git.json.limits: Filesystem measurement of one package; not a claim about installer compression.

measurement-final.json.proves: Real cold/warm start, offscreen first frame, engine import/build/probe waits, 900 headless frames, process memory, package and installer size, git log/diff P50/P95 over 30 runs and synthetic 1k/10k asset-index calibration, each with threshold and verdict.
measurement-final.json.limits: Measured against the round-one package, before the Git tree was bundled; candidate-apply, install and product asset search/preview are skipped.

measurement.txt.proves: Readable metric table plus skipped/unmeasured reasons.

product-rpc-r1.json.proves: The measurement wiring works against a real R1 debug build over stdio JSON-RPC: hello round trip and 10 content.gitInfo round trips (p50 ~0.11 ms, p95 ~65 ms). asset.search returns UNKNOWN_METHOD there.
product-rpc-r1.json.limits: R1 is not integrated and this is a debug build of a task branch; the numbers are calibration and their thresholds stay pending-real-sample.

product-rpc-r1.txt.proves: Readable table plus the skipped asset.search reason.

product-rpc-r6.json.proves: The same wiring against R6's debug build: hello and 10 content.gitInfo round trips; asset.search is UNKNOWN_METHOD in that build too, so the product asset path stays pending.
product-rpc-r6.json.limits: Task-branch debug build, not integrated; calibration only.

product-rpc-r6.txt.proves: Readable table plus the skipped asset.search reason.
